evidence: Grad-CAM encoder with attention mining loss; state-of-the-art on several unnamed datasets; ablation studies
rationale: Lowercase 'improve' read as outcome-verb title (imperative reading would be 2). SOTA on several datasets supports it; abstract claims stay within its vague evidence.

evidence: Euclidean TSP; trained on TSP-100; state-of-the-art up to 10,000 cities vs sparsification-based neural solvers
rationale: 'Solving TSP' asserts a solution; evidence is SOTA neural results on Euclidean TSP only. Concluding claim extends to all neural combinatorial optimization.

evidence: Formal proofs: MaxEnt RL optimally solves a class of POMDPs; equivalence to two-player game with adversarial reward
rationale: Question title answered by theorems for specific problem classes, not broadly enough for understated. Implications are hedged (suggest, might).

evidence: Session-pair encoder with latent proximity constraint; transfer to unnamed downstream tasks; comparable to several industrial baselines
rationale: Title implies improvement, but evidence shows only parity with industrial baselines. Abstract asserts better representations across tasks without reported gains.

evidence: Various unnamed MLLMs and datasets; removing cues lowers accuracy; hallucination amplified over 10x; robustness checks; prompting mitigations; ablations
rationale: Descriptive name title. Causal failure-mode claims rest on cue-removal interventions and robustness checks; claims stay within reported findings.

evidence: MMD string-kernel test: 77.4% median power, ~10 samples per prompt; four Llama models, 31 commercial endpoints, 11 differ
rationale: Question title; evidence firmly tests API-versus-reference equality. Abstract claims match reported numbers.

evidence: Mask-based attribution-prior training methods; expert-masked images; covariate shift; generalization gains not tracking attribution correction
rationale: Hedged sentence title ('possible red herring') scored 2; matches finding of no strong attribution-generalization correspondence. Conclusions are hedged.

evidence: STAMP vs recent pruning methods on unnamed benchmark datasets; better compression at similar accuracy; orders-of-magnitude faster training
rationale: 'Rapid' supported by orders-of-magnitude faster training. Claim of generalizing to 'any unseen datasets' exceeds the benchmark evaluation.

evidence: CamVid, Cityscapes; single-frame baseline and prior work; 20+ fps at 960x720; ~6x and 2.5x speedups; competitive accuracy
rationale: 'Fast' backed by reported frame rates and speedups on two named datasets; 'substantially' accompanied by numbers.

evidence: BERT classifier on Korean postpositions -ey, -eyse, -(u)lo; accuracy vs number of functions, corpus size, training epochs
rationale: Question title answered by reported accuracy patterns. Claim that BERT simulates human interpretation has no reported human comparison.

evidence: Minimax proofs in nonparametric binary classification under label shift and group-covariate shift (small overlap); one label-shift dataset case study
rationale: Optimality title backed by theorems and scoped to nonparametric classification; small-overlap condition omitted but core holds. Abstract stays within theory.

evidence: Simulation and real robots; differing modality, physics, morphology; real-arm video aligned to simulated arm without paired data
rationale: Activity-gerund title. Abstract reports experiments across stated domain pairs; transfer claims are unquantified but not beyond reported settings.

evidence: NARF with two unnamed CDR algorithms; synthetic and large real-world datasets; outperforms baselines
rationale: Topic title. Unquantified 'significantly outperforms' is only a booster; noise-mechanism motivation is framing, not a central overreach.

evidence: Unnamed long-text tasks; outperforms full KV cache using 50% of cache; no fine-tuning; CGE and RGL eviction strategies
rationale: 'Big difference' matched by reported 50% cache with better performance. 'Integrates seamlessly with existing LLMs' and 'consistently' exceed the unnamed evaluation.

evidence: Range of GANs incl. SNGAN, CycleGAN; matching subnetworks at 67-74% sparsity; transfer to unseen tasks; beats prior GAN compression
rationale: Existence claim 'GANs can' supported across a range of GANs. 'First time' is scoped to this study; boosters accompany named results.

evidence: Llama 3.2 1B; unlearning seven Harry Potter novels; unlearning metrics improve; more PII regurgitation, amplified under red-teaming
rationale: Title is scoped to Llama 3.2 1B and matches findings. Abstract asserts a mechanism (shift toward memorized remnants) without reported mechanistic evidence.

evidence: FineDA on unnamed standard ZSDA benchmarks and in-house surgical dataset with smoke, blood, low lighting
rationale: 'Fine-grained' and 'context-aware' are descriptive design attributes, so title scored 0. Effectiveness claims are general but tied to reported benchmarks.

evidence: BadVLMDriver on two VLMs, five trigger objects, two backdoor behaviors; 92% attack success for sudden acceleration with red balloon
rationale: 'Can jeopardize' matched by 92% success. 'Significant real-world threat' and stealth in diverse scenarios exceed reported model-level experiments.

evidence: Paired structured/semi-structured tables; diagnostic splits by size, joins, complexity, schema quality; SQL-based, LLM, hybrid methods
rationale: Descriptive title. 'First controlled study' is a qualified priority claim; trade-off findings stay within the controlled comparison.

evidence: Larger-model guidance: up to +24 on GSM8K (7B); QuestCoT gains on GSM8K, SVAMP, ASDiv, MultiArith across several small models
rationale: Evaluative noun phrase ('advantage', 'importance') supported by guidance and QuestCoT gains on four named datasets; 'all models' refers to tested models.

evidence: Transformers vs LSTMs on noisy k-sparse parity, majority, random k-juntas; sensitivity analysis; simplicity-bias trap; sensitivity-penalty loss
rationale: Conditional failure title matches k-junta results and trap experiment. Conclusion that transformers are ineffective for boolean functions ignores reported parity/majority successes.

evidence: RUBICON vs TD3/TD3+BC baselines; building-RL environments, multiple tasks and weather conditions; +40.7% offline, +49.7% online reward
rationale: Topic title. Performance claims are quantified and scoped to building-RL environments; no overreach.

evidence: PH-Dropout on pre-trained NeRF and GS models; unspecified 'extensive evaluations'; no datasets, timings or accuracy numbers
rationale: 'Practical' rests on asserted real-time accuracy, but no timing or accuracy evidence is reported. 'First real-time and accurate method' likewise unsupported.

evidence: Batch size varied up to full batch; Adam-SGD gap persists and grows; simpler SGD variants; Adam resembles sign descent with momentum
rationale: Negative causal claim backed by full-batch experiments; sign-descent part hedged ('might'). Abstract frames findings as 'evidence'.

evidence: ResNets on CIFAR10, ImageNet; ResNet50 75.02% top-1 at 80% pruning in 22% epochs; memorization analysis; too-early pruning degrades accuracy
rationale: 'The sooner the better' is qualified by the abstract's own finding that pruning before weight saturation degrades accuracy. Abstract claims tied to named results.

evidence: DAGGER-trained policy imitating best AL heuristic; batch-mode pool-based setting; unnamed well-known datasets; beats SOTA imitation learners and heuristics
rationale: Descriptive title. Outperformance claim stated at the level of the reported comparison; no overreach.

evidence: Unspecified experiments showing content incorporation into generated text and zero-shot attribute control
rationale: Descriptive title. Abstract claims match its unquantified experimental statements; absence of numbers is not overreach.

evidence: Theory and simulations with a-priori set polarities; image classification transfer via polarity vs weights; cases where fixed polarity hurts
rationale: 'All you need' contradicted by the abstract's own disadvantageous cases. Abstract also explains biological polarity stability and claims value for NI without biological evidence.

evidence: Unnamed RL tasks with varied physical parameters; curriculum matches exhaustive grid-search best policies at lower computational cost
rationale: Purpose-clause title supported: method matches most-robust grid-search policies. Claims scoped to the considered tasks.

evidence: CNN image classification; privacy loss vs accuracy across local NN topologies; CIFAR-10
rationale: 'Flexible' supported by topology selection under privacy, compute and storage constraints. Abstract restricts its demonstration to CIFAR-10.

evidence: Unspecified empirical study; improves accuracy of current SOTA samplers; reduces redundancy error; pruning visualizations
rationale: Acronym plus activity gerund ('Learning to prune'). Hedged claims ('could augment') stay within vague evidence.

evidence: Constructed distribution: orthogonal-invariant algorithms need Omega(d^2) samples vs O(1) for CNNs; target-function gap; l2 regression; Adam, AdaGrad
rationale: Question title answered by a provable separation on one natural distribution; claims track theorem assumptions.

evidence: 7.8x average speedup vs DyGLib across models, datasets, tasks; 175x discretization speedup; enables dynamic graph property prediction
rationale: 'Efficient' matched by reported speedups. 'Entirely new research possibilities... previously impractical' is a sweeping novelty claim beyond the reported demonstrations.

evidence: Six zero-shot benchmarks (object, intent, fine-grained entity typing); +1.7 over specialized SOTA, +5.3 over general method; ablation +2.8
rationale: Descriptive title. SOTA and general-purpose claims scoped to six benchmarks across three task types with numbers.

evidence: ATOM; classic and adversarial OOD tasks; CIFAR-10 in-distribution: FPR95 reduced up to 57.99% vs previous best
rationale: Title matched by outlier-mining gains. SOTA 'under a broad family' and generalization to unseen attacks rest on one reported in-distribution dataset.

evidence: Mixture-of-experts data selection from a dataserver; SOTA on several unnamed target datasets for classification, detection, instance segmentation
rationale: Question-style title answered by the proposed selection method. SOTA claims scoped to named tasks; no overreach.

evidence: Theory: optimal adversary for fixed policy; learned-adversary attack; ATLA training; LSTM policies; few continuous control environments, SOTA under strong adversaries
rationale: Evaluative attributes ('Robust', 'Optimal') backed by optimal-adversary theory and SOTA under attacks. 'Much stronger' unquantified but not overreach.

evidence: Generator-Defender adversarial training (IRGAN-inspired loss); comparison with unspecified static defenses; no datasets, models or numbers
rationale: 'Robust' matches reported resilience vs static defenses. Resilience to 'novel and evolving threats' and 'critical foundation' exceed the thin reported evidence.

evidence: Two post-hoc correction techniques on standard-trained models; bias localized to classification layer; unspecified empirical verification
rationale: Question title answered with hedged evidence ('in certain settings', 'may'); claims stay within reported scope.

evidence: LSTM representations pretrained on large datasets, transferred to small forecasting tasks; M3 and other datasets; beats majority of best methods
rationale: 'Universal' forecaster exceeds M3-plus-others evaluation. 'First time'/'no prior work' is sweeping novelty; future tool claims exceed evidence.

evidence: Within-class isometric regularization during classification; adversarial robustness on MNIST
rationale: Generic title from one MNIST adversarial test. Abstract claims benefits for robust inferences 'about the world' and an architecture for the community beyond evidence.

evidence: 20 LLMs, three benchmarks; selection bias traced to option-ID token bias; PriDe label-free inference-time debiasing
rationale: Generic claim about LLMs backed by 20 models and three benchmarks; causal attribution supported by reported analyses.

evidence: Tree positional encodings; tree-to-tree program translation and sequence-to-tree semantic parsing; beats vanilla transformer on several tasks
rationale: 'Novel' plus purpose clause 'to enable' supported by working tree transformers outperforming the vanilla transformer.

evidence: WT-AWP regularization; unnamed graph learning tasks and GNN models; natural and robust generalization gains; vanishing-gradient analysis
rationale: Title claim about AWP supported via the WT-AWP variant across many tasks and models; unquantified but not overreach.

evidence: MSTAR benchmark; beats DCN with 3% of its parameters; matches SurReal with 40% of its parameters
rationale: Descriptive title. 'Much leaner' is quantified; 'better generalization' loosely matches results on one dataset.

evidence: Minimax lower bound: any algorithm needs poly(1/eps) training domains; DomainBed: OOD accuracy rises monotonically with domain count
rationale: Causal title backed by lower-bound theorem plus DomainBed trend; recommendations hedged ('suggests').

evidence: PHIER on CALVIN and BEHAVIOR; few-shot OOD state classification vs existing methods; sim-to-real zero/few-shot generalization
rationale: Title supported by PHIER gains in two named environments; hierarchy's isolated effect not reported, but the method is hierarchy-centred.

evidence: Proof AUL unbiased in PU learning; 9 datasets: AUL error 1/6 of AUC; vs SOTA AUC optimizer: lower cost, up to 10% gain
rationale: Comparative title backed by a proof and quantified nine-dataset experiments.

evidence: Proofs for zero-sum bilinear games and normal matrices; disk-eigenvalue speed-up vs worst-case optimal; benchmarks with assumption mismatch
rationale: 'Average-case acceleration' treated as a topic name (0, not outcome nominalization). Claims are theorem-backed and scoped.

evidence: 1,000 samples, 10 subjects, four-level taxonomy; GPT-Image-1, Gemini-2.5-Flash-Image under 15% strict; most models near 0%
rationale: Descriptive title. 'Rigorous assessment' of integrated abilities and 'insights on the path to AGI' exceed reported benchmark scores.
